summary: Specifies the Character Generator service, which sends data without regard to the input. It is an Internet Standard for hosts that choose to implement it.

eli5.summary: A computer that keeps sending out letters, no matter what you say, like a never-ending ticker tape.

questions: what is the character generator protocol
how does chargen work over udp
subtitle: A service that streams meaningless but recognizable text, useful for testing networks.

tldr.problem: Engineers need a simple source of data to debug and measure a network connection, without having to supply input.
tldr.mechanism: A server on port 19 sends data and ignores whatever it receives. Over TCP it streams until the user disconnects; over UDP it answers each datagram with a random number of characters between 0 and 512.
tldr.outcome: The RFC is an Internet Standard for hosts that choose to implement it. It also recommends a rotating pattern of the 95 ASCII printing characters in 72-character lines.

today: RFC 864 is an Internet Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated, so it remains the definition of the Character Generator Protocol.

sections.title: A Character Generator Service
sections.content:
RFC 864 defines the Character Generator Protocol (chargen). The RFC calls a character generator a useful debugging and measurement tool: it simply sends data without regard to the input.

Hosts on the ARPA Internet that choose to implement it are expected to adopt this standard. Implementing it is optional.
sections.eli5: It is a machine that just keeps talking, whatever you tell it. That makes it handy for testing whether a line is working.

sections.title: The TCP and UDP Services
sections.content:
Over TCP, a server listens on TCP port 19. Once a connection is established it sends a stream of data and throws away anything it receives. This continues until the calling user terminates the connection. Users may abruptly abort instead of closing carefully, so the service should be prepared for either a careful close or a rude abort. Normal TCP flow control keeps the service from sending faster than the user can process.

Over UDP, a server listens on UDP port 19. For each datagram received it sends one answering datagram containing a random number (between 0 and 512) of characters, and the received data is ignored. The UDP version keeps no history or state, so there is no continuity of data from one answering datagram to the next.
sections.eli5: With TCP the machine pours out letters until you hang up. With UDP it sends back one random-sized handful of letters each time you knock.

sections.title: Data Syntax and the Rotating Pattern
sections.content:
The data may be anything, but the RFC recommends a recognizable pattern. One popular pattern uses 72-character lines of the ASCII printing characters. There are 95 printing characters; sort them and number them 0 through 94, treating the sequence as a ring so that character 0 follows character 94.

Line 0 holds characters 0 through 71, line 1 holds characters 1 through 72, and so on. Line N holds characters (0+N mod 95) through (71+N mod 95). Each line ends with a carriage return and line feed. The effect is a diagonal pattern that makes dropped or garbled data easy to spot.
sections.eli5: Each line is the line before it, slid over by one letter, wrapping around at the end. If anything goes missing, the pattern looks wrong.
